notes.title: A quieter week before Iceland
lookBack: **248 WaniKani reviews this week**, mostly in two days: 122 on Tuesday, then 41 on Friday and 41 on Saturday, with none on Thursday and none so far today. Accuracy stayed where it's been, about **84% on meanings and 89% on readings**. You started 5 new lessons on Wednesday. Nothing burned this week, which is expected: last week's big push cleared everything that was close. The queue is at 93 going into the trip.

Grammar didn't move. は vs が is still the only lesson marked done (and solid, 10 of 12 right). Lessons 2–4 are still waiting. Of the 16 verb-pair drills, you've tried 2 (vp01 once right, once wrong; vp02 right), so it's too early to say whether they're working. Last week's set stays up, and I didn't write a new one. You also finished one Noriko story (4 minutes).
noticed: **Meanings trail readings by 5 points**, and your leeches show why. 見せる, 交じる, 失う, 出かける, 明かり: you can read them but don't know which is which. 出かける reached Guru and 回す dropped off the leech list on their own, so the verb pairs are starting to settle. 見せる is still stuck, which is why this week's lesson and drills use 見える vs 見せる again.

**You're now four lessons ahead of what you've marked done** (2, 3, 4 and this week's 5). So next week I'll stop adding chapters and deepen these instead: more drills and more of their grammar in scenes, so you meet it in context first. Marking one lesson done is worth more right now than reading a new one.

**This week's lesson is the potential form** (話せる, 食べられる, できる). It's the grammar behind 日本語が少し話せます, the line that tells a stranger they can talk to you. The Dinner as a guest scene has a new natural tier built on it, which opens when you mark Lessons 1 and 5 done.
focus: **Mark Lesson 2 (に vs で) done this week.** Read it on the plane. It's short, and three new review drills are already waiting for it.
**Iceland rhythm, about two hours a day:** reviews and lessons in the morning; one Daily practice and one Vault reading in the afternoon (this week: a northern sea town, a radio show, a tea house).
**Five verb-pair drills a day from the 先生 page** until you've done all 16. They're aimed at 見せる, the leech that's still stuck.
**Listen with no subtitles at all, five minutes a day.** Start with Noriko's Markus 3/4 (3 minutes). The listenFor on each pick gives you one thing to catch, so you're never just lost.

notes.jaEn: Even in Iceland, let's think in Japanese a little every day. By March, I'm sure you'll be able to talk at a bar.

notes.title: The backlog is (nearly) gone
lookBack: **You did it.** Two weeks ago your queue stood at 948. Today it's 65, after your biggest day yet (147 reviews). Burned items went from 450 to 957 over those two weeks, 113 of them this week. That pile was mostly items one step from burned, and you finished it.

The rest of the week was steady: 30 to 56 reviews most days, one day off on Wednesday, and almost nothing the weekend before. That's fine, since the whole hub is built so a missed day doesn't pile up. Accuracy held: about **84% on meanings and 86% on readings** this week.
noticed: **Your leeches are mostly verb pairs.** 見せる vs 見る, 出かける vs 出る, 回す vs 回る: you're missing the meaning, not the reading. That's transitive vs. intransitive ("I turn it" vs. "it turns"), and it's exactly the next chapter in your grammar course. One lesson there will probably fix several leeches at once.

**The vocabulary is outrunning the grammar.** You've burned hundreds of words, but only は vs が is in your grammar reviews (10 of 12 right, solid). Lessons 2 and 3 are waiting. Grammar is what turns a pile of words into sentences you can say at a bar.
Daily practice and Glue haven't been opened yet. That's no surprise, since reviews took every spare minute, but this is the week that changes.
focus: **Start lessons, gently.** Your queue is under 100, so the Lessons card on Today is open. Follow its budget (about 10 a day) and watch for the ✈ and ◆ flags.

**Verb-pair drills (処方).** I wrote 16 exercises aimed at your leeches: 見せる/見る, 出かける/出る/出す, 回す/回る and the pairs around them. Three a day show up in Daily practice, or run them all from the 先生 page. The rule that makes them click is in the drill set: look at the particle, not the meaning.
**One Daily practice a day.** Seven minutes, mostly glue words. It's the part of the hub that trains you to sound like you're talking.

**Read Lesson 2 (に vs で) before Iceland,** and mark it done. The transitive/intransitive lesson your leeches were asking for is now up as **Lesson 4 (出す vs 出る)**, with 12 review drills on 見せる/見る, 出かける/出る and 回す/回る. The Rehearsal scene has a new natural tier built on it (音が出ません, マイクを向けてください) that opens once Lessons 2–4 are marked done.

**Iceland starts Monday the 26th.** With two hours a day there, the plan is: reviews and lessons in the morning, Daily practice and one Vault reading in the afternoon, and a Claude role-play from a scene when you want to talk.
